criteria.revision: Open with the less expected trigger-response wording: "When Meowth sees a shiny object, the gold coin on its head shines too." Then delay the picking habit until later.

criteria.quote: At night, Meowth searches streets for dropped loose change.
What else happens when Meowth spots something shiny?
criteria.revision: Make the question drive the sequence: begin with "Meowth searches the streets at night for shiny things—but what happens when it finally spots one?" Reveal the eyes, coin, and picking behavior in separate beats.

criteria.quote: See a shiny object, and the gold coin on its head shines.
criteria.revision: Reorder the existing evidence so each beat adds a new reaction: nighttime searching, glittering eyes, the shining coin, then the inability to stop picking shiny things up. Add the documented fights with Murkrow over shiny objects as the final escalation.

criteria.quote: When Meowth spots shine, its eyes glitter brightly too.
criteria.revision: Do not reveal the coin shine in the title, premise, or first scene. Establish the eyes and picking habit first, then reveal: "When it sees a shiny object, the gold coin on its head shines too."

criteria.quote: Its coin shines at shiny objects.
criteria.revision: Remove the repeated coin beats from the first and third scenes. Give each scene one distinct fact: night searching, glittering eyes, coin shining, picking objects up, and fighting Murkrow over shiny objects.

criteria.quote: One shiny sight connects Meowth's coin, glittering eyes, and picking habit.
criteria.revision: End with a stronger synthesis: "One shiny object makes Meowth's eyes glitter, its coin shine, and its paws reach for it—because it can't stop picking shiny things up."
Use a clearer evidence-grounded split: "Is the coin shine the strangest part—or is Meowth's inability to stop picking up shiny things?"
